subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a core per-agent or grouped foreground command-lane config surface, and what server-controlled safety contract should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes scheduler isolation, public config, upgrade expectations, and adjacent lane semantics rather than repairing a single broken contract.

options.title: Design Config-Driven Foreground Lanes
options.body: Add a trusted default-preserving config surface for foreground agent lane selection and per-lane concurrency, with an aggregate safety cap and upgrade tests.

options.title: Fold Into A Scheduler RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers design one lane/concurrency model covering foreground agents, hooks, subagents, browser-heavy work, and channel-specific routing.

options.title: Prefer Separate Gateway Isolation
options.body: Document separate gateway instances as the supported isolation pattern and decline a core foreground lane config until demand or design constraints change.

recommendation.title: Design Config-Driven Foreground Lanes
recommendation.body: Add a trusted default-preserving config surface for foreground agent lane selection and per-lane concurrency, with an aggregate safety cap and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current foreground lane and embedded runtime files point to this person as the best available code-history owner for the scheduler/config decision.
